subject.title: Transcript redaction corrupts Anthropic/Bedrock reasoning signatures (AIza/LTAI false positive), causing persistent replay_invalid

question: Should provider-owned Anthropic/Bedrock reasoning signature fields bypass secret-pattern redaction based on route and opaque-token shape even when the byte string contains a credential-looking substring?
rationale: The current tests intentionally redact credential-shaped values on provider signature fields, but the issue shows that this idempotency gate can corrupt real provider signatures; automation should not choose that security boundary alone.

options.title: Adopt route-scoped opaque-token preservation
options.body: Preserve validated opaque signatures only in provider-owned assistant reasoning slots, and keep normal redaction for user text, nested payloads, route-missing data, malformed data, and ellipsis-marked values.

options.title: Prefer send-side recovery only
options.body: Keep the current credential-first redaction boundary and add Bedrock/Anthropic replay guards to drop corrupted signatures, accepting that stored signatures may still be poisoned.

options.title: Defer as adjacent replay work
options.body: Treat this as part of the broader invalid-signature replay cluster, but that leaves the source-level corruption mechanism open until a canonical owner takes it.

recommendation.title: Adopt route-scoped opaque-token preservation
recommendation.body: Preserve validated opaque signatures only in provider-owned assistant reasoning slots, and keep normal redaction for user text, nested payloads, route-missing data, malformed data, and ellipsis-marked values.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily a redaction/security-boundary choice, and recent secrets work makes steipete the best available routing owner from the inspected history.
